_inspectorSnowReport.Report:
Saturday March 21 | 5:30 a.m 

Bonjour Tremblant!

Spring is finally here, and what a way to celebrate it! The mountain is looking its absolute best today. The forecast is gorgeous with the sun is peaking through this morning and temperatures creeping into the positives at the base. It is shaping up to be a spring skiing day at its finest! An additional 3 cm fell over the last 24 hours, adding to Friday's incredible 12 cm dump, and the terrain across the mountain is, as a result, in very good shape! The Glades are also riding beautifully. If you've been waiting for the right day to duck in, today is the day!

Moreover, all 4 Terrain Parks are dialed in, and speaking of parks, Jamigos is happening TODAY in Parc Adrénaline! Come test out brand new modules and set-ups while soaking in the sunshine and prime spring conditions. It's going to be a great atmosphere out there!

First Tracks access begins as early as 7:45 a.m. on both North and South side, with North Side slopes opening at 8 a.m. With a sunrise like today's, there's nowhere else you'd want to be. Heads up, First Tracks wraps up tomorrow, Sunday March 22, so this morning is one of your last chances to experience it. Don't let it slip by!

Ontario Spring Break, join us this evening at Place St-Bernard for activities from 2:30 to 9:00 p.m. A perfect way to cap off a perfect spring day on the mountain.
Get here early, stay late, and make the most of this one. Days like today are what it's all about!

Mountain safety tip of the week: Après-ski is after skiing!
Do NOT use ski lifts or ski runs if you are under the influence of drugs or alcohol.
This is required under the Mountain Code of Conduct.
Stay Sharp on the Slopes
  • Collisions and falls increase when your concentration, awareness, and reaction time are reduced.
  • Drugs and alcohol impair your abilities on the slopes just like they do on the road.
  • Protect yourself and others—ski responsibly.
Snow fall is recorded daily at 5 a.m from mid-mountain at North Side (550 m / 1,800 ft). This data, based on 24 hours, provides a picture of on-mountain conditions. Actual accumulation may differ from the official report. Be aware of changing conditions. Lifts and trails exist in a mountain environment and may close due to weather, usage and/or special maintenance.
